## R Markdown

```{r}
#Install it if you haven't.
library(guardianapi)
```

```{r}
#Enter your Guardian API key.
gu_api_key()
```

```{r}
#Find contents with required keywords and period.
fraud <- gu_content(query = '"fraud" AND ("UK" OR "United Kingdom")', from_date = "1999-01-01",
                            to_date = "2024-12-31")
```

```{r}
#Find contents for comparing with forecasts.
fraud1 <- gu_content(query = '"fraud" AND ("UK" OR "United Kingdom")', from_date = "2025-01-01",
                            to_date = "2025-12-31")
```

```{r}
#Inspect the articles obtained.
tibble::glimpse(fraud)
```

# Count the number of articles published each month

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

monthly_fraud <- fraud %>%
  filter(type == "article",
         pillar_name %in% c("Lifestyle", "News", "Opinion")) %>%
  mutate(month = floor_date(as.Date(web_publication_date), unit = "month")) %>%
  count(month, name = "n_articles")

monthly_fraud

# Save to a csv
write.csv(monthly_fraud,
          file = "fraud_train.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# Also for the tested contents.
monthly_fraud1 <- fraud1 %>%
  filter(type == "article",
         pillar_name %in% c("Lifestyle", "News", "Opinion")) %>%
  mutate(month = floor_date(as.Date(web_publication_date), unit = "month")) %>%
  count(month, name = "n_articles")

monthly_fraud1

# Save to a csv
write.csv(monthly_fraud1,
          file = "fraud_test.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
```

# Import fraud and macroeconomic data (treat n_articles as fraud)

```{r}
# Import the training dataset
train <- read.csv("fraud&macroeconomic_train.csv")
View(train)

# Import the testing dataset
test <- read.csv("fraud&macroeconomic_test.csv")
View(test)
```

```{r}
# Name each time series
fraud <- train$fraud
inflation <- train$CPIH
unemployment <- train$unemployment
interest <- train$interest_rate
production <- train$index_of_production_and_industry_sectors
confidence <- train$composite_consumer_confidence
```

```{r}
# Name variables in the test dataset
fraud_test <- test$fraud
inflation_test <- test$CPIH
unemployment_test <- test$unemployment
interest_test <- test$interest_rate
production_test <- test$index_of_production_and_industry_sectors
confidence_test <- test$composite_consumer_confidence
```

# Cross-correlation analysis to find the lead-lag relationships between variables

```{r}
# Test the stationarity of all time series.
library(tseries)

adf.test(fraud)
adf.test(inflation)
adf.test(unemployment)
adf.test(interest)
adf.test(production)
adf.test(confidence)
```

```{r}
# Take first order differencing to check if non-stationary time series become stationary.
adf.test(diff(unemployment))
adf.test(diff(interest))
adf.test(diff(production))
```

```{r}
#Print cross-correlation functions
ccf(fraud, inflation)
ccf(fraud, diff(unemployment))
ccf(fraud, diff(interest))
ccf(fraud, diff(production))
ccf(fraud, confidence)
#Print cross-correlation values
ccf(fraud, inflation, plot = FALSE)
ccf(fraud, diff(unemployment), plot = FALSE)
ccf(fraud, diff(interest), plot = FALSE)
ccf(fraud, diff(production), plot = FALSE)
ccf(fraud, confidence, plot = FALSE)
```

```{r}
ccf(inflation, diff(unemployment))
ccf(inflation, diff(interest))
ccf(inflation, diff(production))
ccf(inflation, confidence)
ccf(inflation, diff(unemployment), plot = FALSE)
ccf(inflation, diff(interest), plot = FALSE)
ccf(inflation, diff(production), plot = FALSE)
ccf(inflation, confidence, plot = FALSE)
```

```{r}
ccf(diff(unemployment), diff(interest))
ccf(diff(unemployment), diff(production))
ccf(diff(unemployment), confidence)
ccf(diff(unemployment), diff(interest), plot = FALSE)
ccf(diff(unemployment), diff(production), plot = FALSE)
ccf(diff(unemployment), confidence, plot = FALSE)
```

```{r}
ccf(diff(interest), diff(production))
ccf(diff(interest), confidence)
ccf(diff(interest), diff(production), plot = FALSE)
ccf(diff(interest), confidence, plot = FALSE)
```

```{r}
ccf(diff(production), confidence)
ccf(diff(production), confidence, plot = FALSE)
```

# Build generalised additive models

```{r}
library(mgcv)
gam1 <- gam(fraud ~ s(inflation) + s(unemployment) + s(interest) + s(production) + s(confidence))
summary(gam1)
```

```{r}
gam2 <- gam(fraud ~ s(inflation) + s(unemployment) + s(confidence))
summary(gam2)
```


```{r}
gam3 <- gam(fraud ~ s(unemployment) + s(interest) + s(production) + s(confidence))
summary(gam3)
```

```{r}
# Compare gam1 and gam3
AIC(gam1, gam3)
BIC(gam1, gam3)
anova(gam1, gam3, test = "F")
```

```{r}
# Consider tensor product interactions
gam4 <- gam(fraud ~ s(unemployment) + s(interest) + s(production) + s(confidence) + ti(unemployment, production) + ti(production, confidence) + ti(inflation, confidence))
summary(gam4)
```

```{r}
gam5 <- gam(fraud ~ unemployment + s(interest) + s(production) + confidence + ti(unemployment, production) + ti(production, confidence) + ti(inflation, confidence))
summary(gam5)
```

```{r}
gam6 <- gam(fraud ~ unemployment + s(interest) + s(production) + confidence + ti(unemployment, production) + ti(inflation, confidence))
summary(gam6)
```


```{r}
AIC(gam5, gam6)
BIC(gam5, gam6)
anova(gam5, gam6, test = "F")
```

```{r}
# Consider using the linear relationship for production
gam7 <- gam(fraud ~ unemployment + s(interest) + production + confidence + ti(unemployment, production) + ti(inflation, confidence))
summary(gam7)
```

```{r}
gam8 <- gam(fraud ~s(interest) + production + confidence + ti(unemployment, production) + ti(inflation, confidence))
summary(gam8)
```

```{r}
AIC(gam8)
BIC(gam8)
```

# Build Vector Autoregressive Moving Average models

```{r}
# Build VARMA time series
varma_data0 <- cbind(
  fraud,
  inflation,
  unemployment,
  interest,
  production,
  confidence
)

library(tseries)

varma_ts0 <- ts(varma_data0, start = c(1999, 1), frequency = 12)#Starting from the 1st period of 1999, and there are 12 such periods in a year, i.e. 12 months.
plot(varma_ts0)
```

```{r}
#"Confidence" shows non-stationary trend, thus apply differencing.
adf.test(diff(confidence))
```


```{r}
varma_data1 <- cbind(
  fraud[-1], #Since 1st-order differencing removes the first observation, repeat it for other time series.
  inflation[-1],
  diff(unemployment),
  diff(interest),
  diff(production),
  diff(confidence)
)

varma_ts1 <- ts(varma_data1, start = c(1999, 2), frequency = 12)#Starting from the 2st period of 1999.
plot(varma_ts1)
```

```{r}
# Determine the autoregressive order p, using values from 1 to 30.
library(vars)

VARselect(varma_data1, lag.max = 30, type = "const")
#p = 1 or 4 is suggested
```

```{r}
install.packages("MTS")
library(MTS)
```

```{r}
# Fit VARMA.
full10 <- VARMA(varma_data1, p = 1, q = 0)
full11 <- VARMA(varma_data1, p = 1, q = 1)
full12 <- VARMA(varma_data1, p = 1, q = 2)
full13 <- VARMA(varma_data1, p = 1, q = 3)
```

```{r}
full40 <- VARMA(varma_data1, p = 4, q = 0)
full41 <- VARMA(varma_data1, p = 4, q = 1)
full42 <- VARMA(varma_data1, p = 4, q = 2)
full43 <- VARMA(varma_data1, p = 4, q = 3)
```

```{r}
c(full10$aic, full10$bic)
c(full11$aic, full11$bic)
c(full12$aic, full12$bic)
c(full13$aic, full13$bic)
c(full40$aic, full40$bic)
c(full41$aic, full41$bic)
c(full42$aic, full42$bic)
c(full43$aic, full43$bic)
# Select full10 and full 40.
```

```{r}
# Use only macroeconomic indicators with significant cross-correlations with fraud.
varma_data2 <- cbind(
  fraud[-1], #Since 1st-order differencing removes the first observation, repeat it for other time series.
  inflation[-1],
  diff(unemployment),
  diff(confidence)
)
```

```{r}
VARselect(varma_data2, lag.max = 30, type = "const")
```

```{r}

part12 <- VARMA(varma_data2, p = 1, q = 2)
part13 <- VARMA(varma_data2, p = 1, q = 3)
```

```{r}
part22 <- VARMA(varma_data2, p = 2, q = 2)
part23 <- VARMA(varma_data2, p = 2, q = 3)
```

```{r}
part40 <- VARMA(varma_data2, p = 4, q = 0)
part41 <- VARMA(varma_data2, p = 4, q = 1)
part42 <- VARMA(varma_data2, p = 4, q = 2)
part43 <- VARMA(varma_data2, p = 4, q = 3)
```

```{r}
c(part10$aic, part10$bic)
c(part11$aic, part11$bic)
c(part12$aic, part12$bic)
c(part13$aic, part13$bic)
c(part20$aic, part20$bic)
c(part21$aic, part21$bic)
c(part22$aic, part22$bic)
c(part23$aic, part23$bic)
c(part40$aic, part40$bic)
c(part41$aic, part41$bic)
c(part42$aic, part42$bic)
c(part43$aic, part43$bic)

```

```{r}
# Forecasting
pred1 <- VARMApred(
  full10,
  h = 12
)
```

```{r}
# Convert differences to their original values, starting from the last value of the training dataset.
pred1$pred[, 3] <- unemployment[length(unemployment)] + cumsum(pred1$pred[, 3])
pred1$pred[, 4] <- interest[length(interest)] + cumsum(pred1$pred[, 4])
pred1$pred[, 5] <- production[length(production)] + cumsum(pred1$pred[, 5])
pred1$pred[, 6] <- confidence[length(confidence)] + cumsum(pred1$pred[, 6])
pred1$pred[, 3]
pred1$pred[, 4]
pred1$pred[, 5]
pred1$pred[, 6]
```

```{r}
install.packages("forecast")
library(forecast)
```


# Build the Extreme Gradient Boosting model

```{r}
install.packages("xgboost")
library(xgboost)
```

```{r}
# Prepare the training dataset 
train$month <- as.Date(train$month) #Treat months as date variables

library(dplyr)

train_data <- train %>%
  arrange(month) %>%
  mutate(
    inflation_lag1 = lag(inflation, 1), # inflation means CPIH
    inflation_lag4 = lag(inflation, 4),
    unemployment_lag1 = lag(unemployment, 1),
    unemployment_lag21 = lag(unemployment, 21),
    interest_lag1 = lag(interest, 1), # interest means interest_rate
    production_lag1 = lag(production, 1), # production means index_of_production_and_industry_sectors
    confidence_lag1 = lag(confidence, 1) # confidence means composite_consumer_confidence
  ) %>%
  na.omit()      #Clean all rows containing NAs produced by lagging.

head(train_data) #Inspect the training dataset
```

```{r}
# Select the predictor columns
predictor_names <- c(
  "CPIH",
  "unemployment",
  "interest_rate",
  "index_of_production_and_industry_sectors",
  "composite_consumer_confidence",
  "inflation_lag1",
  "inflation_lag4",
  "unemployment_lag1",
  "unemployment_lag21",
  "interest_lag1",
  "production_lag1",
  "confidence_lag1"
)
```

```{r}
# Create the predictor matrix and the response variable
X_train <- as.matrix(train_data[, predictor_names])
y_train <- train_data$fraud
```

```{r}
# Construct xgb.DMatrix object
dtrain <- xgb.DMatrix(
  data = X_train,
  label = y_train
)
```

```{r}
# Train the model
xgb_model <- xgb.train(
  params = xgb.params(objective = "reg:squarederror"), #reggression objective with squared loss
  data = dtrain,
  nrounds = 1000, #maximum of 1000 boosting iterations
  verbose = 1 #it will print information about performance
)
```

# Forecasting

```{r}
# Investigate whether there are seasonal patterns in the macroeconomic indicators
acf(inflation, lag.max = 50)
acf(unemployment, lag.max = 50)
acf(interest, lag.max = 50)
acf(production, lag.max = 50)
acf(confidence, lag.max = 50)
```

```{r}
install.packages("forecast")
library(forecast)
```

```{r}
# Determine the difference order, d
ndiffs(inflation)
ndiffs(unemployment)
ndiffs(interest)
ndiffs(production)
ndiffs(confidence)
```

```{r}
# PACF for determining p, ACF for q, of ARIMA
acf(diff(inflation))
pacf(diff(inflation))
acf(diff(unemployment))
pacf(diff(unemployment))
acf(diff(interest))
pacf(diff(interest))
acf(diff(production))
pacf(diff(production))
acf(diff(confidence))
pacf(diff(confidence))
```

```{r}
fit11 <- arima(inflation, order = c(3,1,0))
fit12 <- arima(inflation, order = c(3,1,1))
fit13 <- arima(inflation, order = c(3,1,2))
fit14 <- arima(inflation, order = c(4,1,0))
fit15 <- arima(inflation, order = c(4,1,1))
fit16 <- arima(inflation, order = c(4,1,2))
AIC(fit11, fit12, fit13, fit14, fit15, fit16)
BIC(fit11, fit12, fit13, fit14, fit15, fit16)#fit13 is used
```

```{r}
fit21 <- arima(unemployment, order = c(2,1,0))
fit22 <- arima(unemployment, order = c(2,1,1))
fit23 <- arima(unemployment, order = c(2,1,2))
AIC(fit21, fit22, fit23)
BIC(fit21, fit22, fit23)#fit21 is used
```

```{r}
fit31 <- arima(interest, order = c(2,1,1))
fit32 <- arima(interest, order = c(3,1,1))
AIC(fit31, fit32)#It suggests fit31, but the difference is very small.
BIC(fit31, fit32)#It suggests fit32, and the difference is more significant. Also there is a spike at lag 3, so fit32 is used.
```

```{r}
fit41 <- arima(production, order = c(2,1,2))
fit42 <- arima(production, order = c(2,1,3))
fit43 <- arima(production, order = c(3,1,2))
fit44 <- arima(production, order = c(3,1,3))
AIC(fit41, fit42, fit43, fit44)#It suggests fit43, but very close to fit41.
BIC(fit41, fit42, fit43, fit44)#It suggests fit41, and fairly much lower than fit43. So fit41 is chosen.
```

```{r}
fit51 <- arima(confidence, order = c(1,1,0))
#fit52 <- arima(confidence, order = c(1,1,1)) #fail to fit
fit53 <- arima(confidence, order = c(2,1,0))
fit54 <- arima(confidence, order = c(2,1,1))
AIC(fit51, fit53, fit54)
BIC(fit51, fit53, fit54)#fit51 is used
```

# Permutation feature importance of the XGBoost model

```{r}
install.packages("iml")
library(iml)
```

```{r}
predictor <- Predictor$new(
    model = xgb_model,
    data = future_data_xgb,
    y = fraud_test,
    predict.function = function(model, newdata)
        predict(model, newdata = xgb.DMatrix(as.matrix(newdata)))
)

set.seed(123) #Set the random state so the results are reproducible

perm_imp <- FeatureImp$new(
    predictor,
    loss = "rmse"
)

plot(perm_imp)

perm_imp$results #numerical results
```
